questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
questions.solution: A circle has an infinite number of lines of symmetry because any line passing through its center will divide it into two identical halves. The other options are incorrect because they suggest a finite or zero number of lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: A square is folded vertically and then horizontally. If a single straight cut is made, which of the following shapes could appear when the paper is unfolded?
questions.solution: A square folded vertically and then horizontally creates four layers. A single straight cut through all layers will result in a square shape when unfolded because the cut will be mirrored across both folds. A circle, triangle, or star would require more complex cuts or folds. The correct answer is a square.

questions.stem: A figure has rotational symmetry with the smallest angle of symmetry as 72°. What is the order of rotational symmetry of the figure?
questions.solution: The order of rotational symmetry is the number of times the figure matches itself in a full 360° rotation. This is calculated by dividing 360° by the smallest angle of symmetry. So, 360° ÷ 72° = 5. The order of rotational symmetry is 5. The other options do not match the calculation of 360° ÷ 72°.
